title: To establish age-appropriate design standards and safety safeguards for artificial intelligence chatbots accessed by minors, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy sets rules for how AI chatbots should be designed so they are safe for minors to use. It also outlines general safety guidelines for chatbots in other contexts.

title: To prohibit Chinese AI models from being used on government-issued devices or software systems, to prohibit the procurement of any such models, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The policy bans the use of Chinese AI models on any government‑issued devices or software systems. It also prohibits the procurement of such models and covers additional related restrictions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a nationwide campaign to raise public awareness and understanding of artificial intelligence. It aims to educate citizens about AI’s benefits and risks, fostering informed decision‑making and responsible technology use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to set up a framework for systematically assessing the safety, security, and ethical risks of AI technologies before they are widely used. It aims to create guidelines and oversight mechanisms so that developers, regulators, and the public can better understand and manage potential harms from AI systems.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: A resolution establishes a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, creating a dedicated group to oversee AI research, development, and regulation. The committee will examine AI risks, benefits, and policy implications to guide lawmakers and stakeholders in shaping responsible AI governance.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed set of regulations designed to set clear rules for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence, with the goal of safeguarding public safety, privacy, and ethical standards. It aims to promote transparency and accountability by requiring impact assessments, disclosure of AI capabilities, and adherence to fairness and bias‑mitigation practices.

title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill would require the Secretary of Defense to set up reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors. It aims to increase oversight and transparency in defense-related AI contracting.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill aims to help workers who lose jobs to automation or AI by offering retraining and support programs. It also requires the federal government to act when unemployment spikes.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution emphasizes that artificial intelligence systems must respect religious freedom and be guided by authoritative texts. It calls for greater transparency in AI development to ensure that these values are upheld.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes to establish an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee AI development, safety, and risk mitigation. It also includes additional provisions and measures related to AI oversight and governance.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard individuals from misleading or false claims made by AI systems, ensuring that consumers receive accurate information about AI capabilities and risks. The legislation requires AI developers and providers to disclose key details, such as the nature of the AI, its intended use, and any potential biases, to promote trust and informed decision‑making.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets out national standards for ensuring that AI systems are rigorously tested, transparent, and safe before deployment. It requires research institutions to follow strict oversight protocols, disclose methodologies, and report outcomes to a federal oversight body.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. This report is intended to provide transparency and oversight regarding the employment of AI in foreign intelligence activities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to strengthen U.S. competitiveness by investing in AI research, development, and training programs. It focuses on expanding access to AI education, creating new workforce opportunities, and ensuring that students, educators, and industry partners are equipped with the skills needed for the rapidly evolving AI economy.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act aims to encourage the creation and use of AI systems that are open source, transparent, and shared widely so that their benefits are more accessible. It also sets standards for safe and responsible AI development, encouraging collaboration and competition among developers while protecting user privacy.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that bars the use of artificial intelligence to diagnose or treat patients without a licensed medical professional’s supervision. It aims to preserve the human element in healthcare and ensure accountability and safety in medical decision‑making.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law aimed at preventing AI companies from artificially raising prices or manipulating wage structures. It seeks to increase transparency, protect consumers, and hold firms accountable for any unfair pricing and wage practices.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to set up a pilot program that uses AI to help defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks, overseen by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s director. The program aims to test and evaluate AI tools for protecting essential services and covers additional related objectives.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and coordinate investigations into cybersecurity incidents and AI-related concerns. The board would review incidents, recommend policy changes, and collaborate with government agencies to enhance national security and responsible AI use.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, a government program to support AI research and development. It also includes additional measures related to AI governance, investment, and policy oversight.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act likely establishes guidelines for the responsible use and transparency of AI models, ensuring they can be read, audited, and understood by stakeholders. It aims to promote trust and accountability by requiring documentation of model behavior and facilitating independent review.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act aims to shield households from the rising electricity bills linked to large AI data centers. It proposes rules and incentives to curb data‑center energy use and help offset the costs that families might otherwise face.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act creates a government agency dedicated to overseeing research, development, and deployment of advanced technology and AI. It sets out policies, funding, and ethical guidelines to guide safe, responsible, and beneficial use of AI across the country.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is aimed at ensuring that any AI systems used in veteran‑related services are developed, deployed, and monitored responsibly. It seeks to protect veterans’ privacy, safety, and fairness by setting standards for accountability, transparency, and oversight when AI technologies are applied to benefits, health care, or support programs.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act proposes new laws to prevent artificial intelligence from acting in ways that could harm people or society. It calls for stricter oversight, mandatory safety standards, and regular audits to ensure AI systems operate within approved guidelines.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that seeks to make sure the artificial intelligence systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs to process veterans’ claims are transparent, reliable, and accountable. It requires the VA to set standards, conduct oversight, and implement safeguards so that veterans are protected from biased or faulty AI decisions.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act bars the use of certain AI systems in high‑risk or sensitive areas, such as national security, critical infrastructure, or financial services. It requires companies to meet strict oversight and accountability standards, and will impose penalties for violations.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act sets rules to ensure that artificial intelligence used in national defense is dependable, safe, and performs as intended. It requires regular reporting on AI system performance and any incidents, so government agencies can monitor and improve AI reliability for security purposes.
